task_instance: Set the timeBuzzer hardware LED to the 'success' status signal (solid green) by invoking the skill's buzzer_led.py CLI, i.e. actually change the color of the physical buzzer LED.
blocker_detail: The skill's sole deliverable is driving a physical timeBuzzer USB-C LED device over MIDI. Its bundled CLI (buzzer_led.py) imports python-rtmidi, opens a MIDI output port whose name contains 'timeBuzzer', and sends MIDI control-change messages on channel 12 (CC 70-78) to set the three RGB LED segments. Accomplishing the core intent requires (a) a physical timeBuzzer device connected via USB, and (b) running Python code with the python-rtmidi package and a live MIDI subsystem. The office-assistant runtime cannot run code at all, and no physical buzzer/MIDI hardware exists in the sandbox, so there is no LED to change and no way to verify any color/effect/signal was applied. These are intrinsic hardware/execution needs, not something to be stubbed or mocked.
evidence: Read /runs/.../skills/r171/timebuzzer-led/SKILL.md: Requirements list a 'timeBuzzer device connected via USB-C' and python-rtmidi; every documented command is a `python3 scripts/buzzer_led.py ...` invocation that outputs to the hardware LED. Read the first 60 lines of scripts/buzzer_led.py (present next to SKILL.md, so not missing): it `import rtmidi`, creates `rtmidi.MidiOut()`, scans `get_ports()` for a port named 'timeBuzzer', and sends MIDI CC bytes (status 187 = channel 12) to segment CCs 70-78 at values 0-127. No file output, no text deliverable, no simulation path exists. The chosen minimal task (signal success -> solid green on the physical LED) cannot be executed or verified without the device and code execution, both of which are outside the granted runtime (read/write/edit text + web). No workaround attempted per the no-stub/no-mock rule.
